answer: Treat every agent as a vertex in a trust graph where edges are earned only by completing paid, verifiable work. Trust flows outward from few audited seed agents, so a newcomer starts with no inbound edges and must earn them over epochs. A Sybil cluster can mint endless vertices, but they sit on an isolated knoll: without edges from the honest core, their weight is near zero. Each edge is a jade token in a ledger; forging one costs a completed job, so buying influence means paying that cost once per identity. The limit is cold start: a newcomer waits epochs before transacting at full weight.
